title: Assistant content from the data directory
description: What the hub uses of the assistant content an extension writes in its own data directory (docs/extensions/extensions.md "Assistant content from the data directory"): assistant.data_status answers, for the calling extension's own data contributions only (no permission needed), what the assistant reads now, what waits to be adopted and why a file is not used. Plugin-side: only the hub and the program speak it.

AssistantDataState.description: What the assistant reads of the contribution: adopted (the content as it is now; skills: sent), pending (instructions: an older version, the new one waits for next_adopt_at), kept (instructions: an older version, the new one cannot be used, see reason), none (nothing: none written yet, none usable, or the extension or contribution is switched off).

AssistantDataReason.description: Why what the assistant reads is not the content as it is now: too_large (over its limit), invalid (not UTF-8 text), not_regular (not a plain file inside the data directory: a directory, or a link out of it), unreadable, rate_limited (a new version of instructions waits for its turn), disabled (the extension is switched off or cannot run), switched_off (this contribution is switched off).

AssistantDataItem.description: One data contribution of the extension.

contribution.description: Its id, as the manifest has it.

path.description: Its file or directory, relative to the data directory.

limit.description: The most it may weigh, in bytes.

bytes.description: What it weighs now (all files, for skills).

detail.description: The rest of a file's problem, for logs.

hash.description: The digest of the content as it is now (instructions: the cleaned text, the first 16 hex digits of its sha256; skills: of every skill's name and digest).

adopted_hash.description: instructions: the digest of the text the assistant reads (for a contribution or extension switched off: read last); empty when that is no text.

adopted_at.description: instructions: when that text was adopted (RFC 3339).

next_adopt_at.description: instructions, state pending: the new version is adopted by then at the latest (RFC 3339); sooner when the hub's own instructions change or the user applies it.
